newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, helped by note auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise, helped by note auction.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were higher in light trading Tuesday afternoon, with most coupons catching a lift from the Treasury's two-year note auction, mortgage experts said.
Pass-throughs generally climbed in tandem with Treasuries and spreads held unchanged to modestly wider, traders said.
"The government market is trading up because the two-year auction went okay, but we've been pretty quiet in mortgages," said one trader at a New York securities firm.
In other activity, traders mentioned glimpsing two bid lists comprising CMO (collateralized mortgage obligation) and ARM (adjustable rate mortgage) issues.
Among key pass-throughs, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 3/32 at 100-29/32, yielding 111 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were up 5/32 at 100-31/32, and Freddie Mac paper rose 6/32 to 101-08/32.
Five-year Treasuries were up 4/32 at 6.72 percent, and 10-year notes were up 8/32 at 6.83 percent.
